decision: Keep the static-first Astro storefront; only price, stock, the bag and the busy level are live
why: Static pages are what make peak traffic fast and cheap; freshness is needed for about five percent of the page.
value: The storefront keeps its speed and cost while telling the truth.

decision: One batched live request per page, micro-cached for about two seconds at the edge with request coalescing
why: Ten thousand people watching one deal should cost one origin read per short window, not ten thousand.
alternative: WebSockets per product, or polling per card.
value: Fresh enough to never sell a gone item, cheap enough for Black Friday.

decision: Stock is shown as bands (In stock, Few left, Sold out) and checked exactly only at reservation
why: Bands are always true and cache well; exact counts at peak are often wrong.
value: Fewer checkout rejections and more trust at the moment of paying.

decision: Add to bag is optimistic when stock is plentiful and confirmed when it is scarce, with an idempotency key per click
why: A false 'added' on a scarce item is the worst experience in retail; on plentiful stock, instant feedback converts.
value: Instant where it's safe, honest where it isn't.

decision: Every extra declares a tier and ships a build-time twin; the busy level only chooses which one shows
why: Degrading must not fetch anything new at the worst possible moment.
alternative: Hide components or show error boundaries.
value: A busy night looks simpler, not broken; layout shift stays 0.

decision: Checkout ships as its own bundle with no third-party tags and is prefetched when the bag opens
why: Marketing tags are the most common peak-day responsiveness regression, and checkout is where it costs money.
value: The path to paying stays light on real phones.
